sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Stablecoins and the future of money: separating functions from instruments
sources.key_claim: Stablecoins grew from under USD 10 billion six years ago to over USD 300 billion; tokenised money market funds roughly doubled in market capitalisation in 2025 to around EUR 7 billion; euro-denominated stablecoins would amplify financial-stability and monetary-transmission risks, and the Eurosystem will offer wholesale settlement via the Pontes project from September with the Appia roadmap targeting an interoperable tokenised ecosystem by 2028.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Stablecoins and the Future of Payments: Evidence from Financial Markets
sources.date_evidence: By Alexander Copestake, Cage Englander, Maria Soledad Martinez Peria, German Villegas-Bauer. March 20, 2026
sources.key_claim: Using high-frequency stock-price variation, the paper estimates that US legislation supporting stablecoins in payments reduced the market value of listed incumbent payment firms by 18 percent, around USD 300 billion, consistent with stablecoins increasing competition in the payments sector.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: How Agentic AI Will Reshape Payments
sources.date_evidence: By Sonja Davidovic, Herve Tourpe. April 24, 2026
sources.key_claim: Agentic AI could shift payments from human-initiated instructions to agent-mediated decisions; the note highlights a tension between probabilistic AI behaviour and the deterministic requirements of payment infrastructure, and concludes that outcomes will depend on institutional design and governance as much as technology.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Banks in the Age of Stablecoins: Some Possible Implications for Deposits, Credit, and Financial Intermediation
sources.date_evidence: December 17, 2025 -- Banks in the Age of Stablecoins: Some Possible Implications for Deposits, Credit, and Financial Intermediation
sources.key_claim: Stablecoin growth can displace bank deposits and shift retail balances into uninsured wholesale deposits, raising deposit concentration and liquidity risk and potentially forcing banks to hold larger liquidity buffers and originate fewer loans.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.publisher: White House Council of Economic Advisers
sources.title: Effects of Stablecoin Yield Prohibition on Bank Lending
sources.date_evidence: Effects of Stablecoin Yield Prohibition on Bank Lending. The White House. April 8, 2026
sources.key_claim: At baseline calibration the CEA model finds that eliminating stablecoin yield raises bank lending by only USD 2.1 billion; even stacking every worst-case assumption produces just USD 531 billion in additional lending, a 4.4 percent rise on 2025Q4 bank loans, under conditions the CEA describes as implausible.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.title: Stablecoin Disintermediation
sources.date_evidence: Staff Reports. Stablecoin Disintermediation. Number 1185. February 2026
sources.key_claim: Using transaction-level data linking on-chain transactions to wholesale interbank payments, the paper documents the first evidence of liquidity-driven bank disintermediation: stablecoins transmit liquidity stress to the banking system, and partner banks' loan share of assets contracts relative to peers.
sources.verbatim_quote: we document the first evidence of liquidity-driven bank disintermediation

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Stablecoins: framing the debate
sources.date_evidence: Pablo Hernandez de Cos, General Manager, Bank for International Settlements. Speech at a Bank of Japan seminar. Tokyo, 20 April 2026
sources.key_claim: As of early April 2026 the global stablecoin market cap was around USD 315 billion against roughly USD 8 trillion in US bank deposits; stablecoin transaction volumes were about USD 35 trillion in 2025 but payment-related flows only around USD 390 billion, and major stablecoins currently operate more like exchange-traded funds than like money, falling short on singleness and interoperability.
sources.verbatim_quote: they currently operate more like exchange-traded funds than like money

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: UK Finance announces live pilot phase to deliver tokenised sterling deposits
sources.date_evidence: The live pilot phase of the UK Finance GBTD project was launched in September 2025.
sources.key_claim: UK Finance launched a live pilot for the first UK transactions of tokenised sterling deposits (GBTD) with Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds, NatWest, Nationwide and Santander, testing person-to-person marketplace payments, remortgaging and digital-asset settlement, running until mid-2026.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: 2026 Diary of Consumer Payment Choice: Consumer habits hold steady as payment options grow
sources.date_evidence: 2026 Diary of Consumer Payment Choice: Consumer habits hold steady as payment options grow. May 11, 2026
sources.key_claim: The 2026 Diary of Consumer Payment Choice finds consumer payment use largely consistent over the past three years; cash remained the third-most-used instrument for the sixth year and was used for about one in seven payments, with four of five consumers using cash in the last 30 days.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Reforming cross-border payments: speech by Andrew Bailey
sources.date_evidence: Reforming cross-border payments - speech by Andrew Bailey. Published on 12 March 2026
sources.key_claim: FSB Chair Andrew Bailey said the G20 is far from reaching its 2027 cross-border payment targets; over half of jurisdictions have extended RTGS hours and over three quarters of fast payment systems are adopting ISO 20022, but improvements for end users remain limited, and new Jurisdiction and Regional Action Plans were announced.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: The digital euro: preparing for a potential launch
sources.date_evidence: The digital euro: preparing for a potential launch. Brussels, 24 March 2026
sources.key_claim: The Eurosystem is continuing technical preparations for the digital euro across inclusion, innovation, ecosystem integration and piloting, and will only consider issuance once EU legislation is in place.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Treasury Proposes Rule to Implement the GENIUS Act's Requirements to Counter Illicit Finance
sources.date_evidence: Treasury Proposes Rule to Implement the GENIUS Act's Requirements to Counter Illicit Finance. April 8, 2026
sources.key_claim: Treasury's FinCEN and OFAC issued a joint proposed rule implementing the GENIUS Act's anti-money-laundering and sanctions-compliance requirements, treating permitted payment stablecoin issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Outlook 2026: Stablecoin fretting will calm down
sources.date_evidence: By Lewis McLellan and John Orchard / 2 January 2026
sources.key_claim: Incumbent banks and central banks are moving to co-opt stablecoins by tokenising their own liabilities; the Bank of England softened its proposed systemic-stablecoin backing from 100 percent unremunerated reserves to 40 percent, and if banks deliver tokenised deposits they could outcompete stablecoins by paying interest while retaining deposit guarantees.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Visa Debuts Agentic Program to Help Banks Test AI Payments
sources.key_claim: Visa launched Visa Agentic Ready, a program letting banks test AI-agent-initiated payments, first in Europe with 21 named issuing partners, and Banco Santander completed a live end-to-end agent-initiated transaction within the program.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: Project Leap phase 2: quantum-proofing payment systems
sources.date_evidence: Project Leap phase 2: quantum-proofing payment systems. Innovation Hub Other | 11 December 2025
sources.key_claim: Project Leap Phase 2 tested post-quantum cryptography in an operational payment system, replacing digital signatures in Eurosystem liquidity transfers, and found significant performance differences between traditional and post-quantum algorithms, underscoring the need for further preparation before migrating the financial system.

sources.topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
sources.title: JP Morgan launches tokenized MMF on Ethereum
sources.date_evidence: JP Morgan launches tokenized MMF on Ethereum. December 15, 2025 by Ledger Insights
sources.key_claim: JP Morgan Asset Management launched its first tokenized money market fund, My OnChain Net Yield Fund, on public Ethereum, seeded with USD 100 million, amid a flurry of similar launches by systemically important banks; BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized fund holds USD 1.8 billion.
